name: Chukot
notes: Cyrillic literary orthography for Chukchi, codified by Skorik (1961/1968, Grammatika chukotskogo yazyka) and described in Dunn (1999), A Grammar of Chukchi. L represents /ɬ/ (Chukchi has no phonemic plain /l/); V is the labial fricative /β/, corrected from an earlier /w/ assumption against NEL gold evidence (вэлёлгын [βeɫ oɫɣən], вамылкалгын [βaməɫkaɫɣən]); R is /ɹ/ (not the retroflex fricative previously assumed). K followed by an apostrophe (K') is an alternate spelling of the uvular stop /q/ (used interchangeably with the dedicated Q-hook letter in dictionaries lacking the special character), not an ejective -- Chukchi has no ejective series. Э and Е are both /e/ in the sampled gold (no orthographic ɛ/e contrast survives); И is /i/ (not /ɪ/); Ы is /ə/ (plain schwa, no breve). Glottal stop is written with an apostrophe, and in at least one sampled soft-sign form the soft sign itself also renders /ʔ/; both map to /ʔ/ here. Ч renders the alveolo-palatal affricate /tɕ/ (attested in the gold, e.g. мачо [matɕo]). Stress is largely rhythmic/iambic and unmarked in the orthography (Dunn 1999); not rule-encoded pending a positional-stress model -- documented exemption, not an oversight. Vowel harmony (dominant/recessive pairs i~e, u~o, schwa~e) governs vowel choice across a word but is not rule-encoded here; each Cyrillic vowel letter maps to its own phoneme regardless of harmony class. This mapping was revised after a NorthEuraLex error-analysis iteration (30-word gold sample) corrected the V, R, K'/apostrophe, Ы, И, Э, and Ч entries from their initial citation-only guesses.
